subject: MDIFF in MIRT with items load exclusively on one dimension

messages.author: 546f31397ff4ae83
messages.subject: MDIFF in MIRT with items load exclusively on one dimension
parts:
Hi there,

I'd like to ask a question about the computation of MDIFF in a bidimensional IRT in which items load only on ONE dimension.   The MDIFF output in the MIRT package seems to give output with b = -d/a.  I read in Reckase that to compute b, one would use b = -d/multidimensional discrimination index.  The multidimensional discrimination index is computed by the squared root of the sum of the squared loadings for all the factors.  Would one use b = -d/a for models with items load exclusively on one dimension, or should one use b =-d/multidimensional discrimination index?  Thanks.

messages.author: 546f31397ff4ae83
messages.subject: Re: MDIFF in MIRT with items load exclusively on one dimension
parts: I'd like to add that I used the second method using the multidimensional discrimination index to compute mdiff and the two sets of mdiff have a correlation of about .5.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: MDIFF in MIRT with items load exclusively on one dimension
parts:
I don't follow why they would be any different. If you have  a simple structure like [a1 0], then MDISC = √ a12 + 02 = a1, so the unidimensional and multidimensional translations of the difficulty parameter will be the same since the denominator is the same (a1 == MDISC). 

Phil
